justification: Frontend display/layout only on the Intelligence Brief page: rewrite the hero subtitle to convey the value proposition (sourced, per-address, full-range) and convert the single-column section stack into a responsive bento grid (3 cols desktop / 2 tablet / 1 mobile) with the headline and field-heavy sections spanning two columns. No data, query, regulatory, or behavioural change — same components, same streaming logic.

pre_impl.existing_data: Section cards rendered in a vertical space-y-3 stack inside a max-w-3xl container, with constraint_arithmetic special-cased to ConstraintArithmeticCard and everything else to SectionCard. The card components and the SSE streaming/parse logic are unchanged.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The single narrow column was lanky for ~13 heterogeneous sections and gave the headline (development capacity) no visual priority. Bento-grid precedent (size signals priority; 3/2/1 responsive) fits a data dashboard better.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No new component or dependency. Reuses the installed shadcn cn() util and Tailwind grid utilities. Adds one pure helper spanFor(section) and wraps each streamed card in a grid cell with a column-span class. Container widened to max-w-6xl; the idle form and error panel capped at max-w-2xl so they stay readable.
pre_impl.external_source_error: No data or network change. spanFor returns a single-column class for any unknown section, so a new or unexpected section key still renders as a normal tile rather than breaking the grid.
pre_impl.frontend_type: Frontend only (TypeScript/React). The streamed card element is typed ReactNode; spanFor returns a string class; cn merges the span with min-w-0 to prevent grid overflow. tsc clean; the only ESLint warning is a pre-existing exhaustive-deps note unrelated to this change.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Before: a tall thin column where the build-capacity headline had no prominence. After: a packed bento grid with the capacity card and the field-heavy planning/environmental sections double-wide, the rest as tiles — scannable, with the headline given spatial weight. Streaming still appends cards; grid-auto-flow:dense packs the uneven heights.

functions.name: spanFor
functions.input: the brief section key for one streamed card, e.g. constraint_arithmetic or economics
functions.output: a Tailwind column-span class string — two columns for headline and field-heavy sections, one column otherwise
functions.if_none: any section key not in the wide set returns the single-column class, so unknown sections render as a normal tile

values: N/A - no regulatory values. The change only controls layout column spans and hero copy; no planning numbers are involved.
queries: N/A - this is a frontend render change; it adds no database or API query and reads only the already-streamed section data.

break_it.scenario: A streamed section key is not one of the recognised wide sections
break_it.what_happens: an unhandled key could throw or produce an undefined span class and break the grid layout
break_it.repro: call spanFor('some_new_section') — it returns the single-column class and the card renders as a normal tile
break_it.how: spanFor checks a fixed Set and returns col-span-1 for anything not in it, so any key is safe

break_it.scenario: A card contains very wide content (long overlay-coverage string) inside a grid cell
break_it.what_happens: without a min-width reset, a wide child can blow out the CSS grid track and break the columns
break_it.repro: code review — each grid cell carries min-w-0 via cn so wide content wraps instead of expanding the track
break_it.how: every grid cell gets min-w-0, the standard fix that lets grid items shrink below content width

break_it.scenario: Cards stream in at very uneven heights and in arbitrary order
break_it.what_happens: a naive grid would leave large vertical gaps below short cards as taller ones arrive
break_it.repro: code review — the grid uses grid-auto-flow:dense with items-start so cards keep natural height and gaps backfill
break_it.how: items-start stops row-height stretch and grid-auto-flow:dense places later small cards into earlier gaps

post_merge.manual_verify: On the Vercel preview, run a brief (e.g. 25 Empire St) and confirm: the new subtitle reads correctly; on desktop the sections form a 3-column bento with the development-capacity card and planning/environmental spanning two columns; it collapses to 2 columns on tablet and 1 on mobile; the idle input and error panel stay narrow; cards still appear progressively. Iterate on spans from the live preview if any section looks under/over-weighted.
